investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-30T16:32–16:39Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-bearing nodes. Because the pod never became schedulable within the eval timeout window (~139–144 s), the agent VM was never created, and all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all concurrent or recently created remote-agent VMs have consumed the full allocatable quota on the 2 kata-capable nodes, leaving no capacity for new pods.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity; if the selector was recently tightened or node labels changed, previously schedulable nodes may now be excluded.

TERTIARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota not reclaimed: leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs or user workloads may be holding the extended resource allocation without an active pod, preventing new scheduling.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-30T16:34–16:39Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across the two eligible nodes. Every attempt to schedule a new remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" on the other 4. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, the eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~139–144 seconds across all three checks before timing out, and the runner never reached the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-30T16:32–16:39Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-bearing nodes. Because the pod never became schedulable within the eval timeout window (~139–144 s), the agent VM was never created, and all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all concurrent or recently created remote-agent VMs have consumed the full allocatable quota on the 2 kata-capable nodes, leaving no capacity for new pods.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity; if the selector was recently tightened or node labels changed, previously schedulable nodes may now be excluded.

TERTIARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota not reclaimed: leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs or user workloads may be holding the extended resource allocation without an active pod, preventing new scheduling.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent demand: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource; if the expected concurrency has grown, the node pool may need to be scaled out.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-30T16:34–16:39Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across the two eligible nodes. Every attempt to schedule a new remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" on the other 4. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, the eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~139–144 seconds across all three checks before timing out, and the runner never reached the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received any response evidence—leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~139–150 s), preventing VM readiness, state polling, and runtime chat from ever executing. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-detected infrastructure failure.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing running pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary: The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, so the 4 other nodes cannot serve as overflow even if they have general compute capacity available.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or other workload may have left orphaned remote-agent pods running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming all vm slots without releasing them — though no cleanup or leak evidence is present in this packet.

Lower probability: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or node-level extended resource configuration was reduced (e.g., fewer peer-pod slots provisioned per node), shrinking total available capacity below the concurrent demand of the eval suite.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message in failed-check.message explicitly names Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes as the blocking condition for all three remote-agents checks.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity / selector configuration for remote-agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector (failed-check.message), concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — all three checks: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (features.json lines 183–185) failed with the same Unschedulable root condition, confirming the entire feature's eval surface is blocked by the scheduling failure.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers pod scheduling. The scheduling failure prevents any downstream evidence collection, causing the contract gap for all 5 required fields.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes immediately to determine current slot utilization and identify which pods are holding vm resource slots.

Check for orphaned or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916), and terminate any that are no longer needed.

If slots are fully consumed by legitimate workloads, assess whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes needs to be increased (e.g., by adding nodes with the required resource or increasing the per-node slot count).

Review the pod node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to determine whether the 4 non-eligible nodes could be made eligible (e.g., by installing the kata peer-pods runtime on additional nodes), reducing concentration risk.
Once cluster capacity is confirmed restored, re-run all three remote-agents eval checks to verify full evidence collection and contract satisfaction before closing this investigation.
Consider adding a pre-flight eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability before attempting agent creation, to surface capacity exhaustion earlier with a clearer diagnostic message.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful remote-agent pod scheduling event on the cluster at the same time as the eval failures would disprove capacity exhaustion as the cause.

kubectl describe node output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes during the failure window would indicate the problem is not capacity but a misconfigured resource request or quota policy.

A passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime with full evidence collected (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) would confirm the cluster has recovered and the failure was transient.
Evidence that the pod affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes would shift the root cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration regression.

Cluster event logs showing the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes were cordoned, drained, or had their extended resource capacity reduced around 2026-06-30T16:34Z would point to a node-level change rather than slot exhaustion by running workloads.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the cluster for available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on affinity-eligible nodes and fails with a capacity warning before any pod creation is attempted.
Add an orphaned-pod cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are left running after the withCleanup phase completes.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with available vm slots), alerting before full exhaustion occurs.
Consider a concurrent-scheduling stress eval that attempts to create two remote-agent pods simultaneously to detect slot contention under the current cluster configuration.
